subject: physics
question_text: Show how a vector is resolved into two perpendicular components. Obtain expressions for its magnitude and direction in terms of these components.

verification.note: PREDICTED — Session 89 enumeration sweep (archetype × object grid over the NCERT chapter): this question has not appeared in any paper or source book we hold, but the chapter contains it and the 2-mark/4-mark format admits it. Authored as a lean card; promote to a full card when a paper season or a Telangana IPE teacher validates the cell. Split invented, as everywhere.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

steps.label: The components
lines: Let a vector A make an angle θ with the
x-axis. Drop perpendiculars from the tip
of A on to the two axes. The two pieces
along the axes are its components A_x, A_y.
steps.margin_note: First mark. Define θ and drop the two perpendiculars before any formula.
steps.why: Resolution is addition run backwards: the two components are the two vectors that would add back to A.
common_mistakes: Drawing the components along any two directions — they must be perpendicular for these formulas.

recall.must_convey: That dropping perpendiculars from the tip of A on to the axes gives the two components A x and A y.
accept: drop perpendiculars on to the axes
reject: A cos theta and A sin theta

steps.memory_tip: A vector and its two components make a right-angled triangle, and A is always the hypotenuse.

steps.label: The two expressions
lines: and A_x i + A_y j builds A back again.
steps.margin_note: Two marks. Both components, and one line showing they add back to A.
steps.why: The cosine goes with the axis the angle is measured FROM — that one habit removes most sign and swap errors.
common_mistakes: Swapping sine and cosine when the angle is measured from the y-axis instead.

recall.must_convey: That A x is A cos theta and A y is A sin theta.
reject: drop perpendiculars on to the axes

steps.memory_tip: Test θ = 0°: the vector lies on the x-axis, A_x = A cos 0 = A and A_y = 0. That fixes which is which.

steps.label: Magnitude and direction

lines.text: A = √(A_x² + A_y²),   tan θ = A_y / A_x

lines: The two components act independently of
steps.margin_note: Fourth mark. Box both results — magnitude and direction are asked for separately.
steps.why: Independence is the useful part: projectile motion works because the horizontal and vertical components never affect each other.
common_mistakes: Writing tan θ = A_x / A_y, the ratio upside down.

recall.must_convey: That A is the root of A x squared plus A y squared, and tan theta is A y over A x.
accept: root of A x squared plus A y squared
tan theta is A y by A x

steps.memory_tip: If θ is less than 45° then A_x is the larger component. Use that to check tan θ = A_y / A_x.

insider_note: A_x = A cos θ and A_y = A sin θ carry 2 of the 4 marks. Draw the labelled right-angled triangle they are read from.
